clue.text: Like a rock when covered by the sea

indicators.note: one thing covered by another sits inside it, so the sea word wraps round the short word

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea of northern Europe
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

explanation.surface: Something resembling stone once the tide has come in over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' looks like a time link but supplies its synonym; the sea is the wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic stone, so an adjective formed from it describes something resembling or made of that stone.

clue.text: Right to jam a signal transmitter in this road

indicators.note: to jam something in is to wedge it inside, so one piece is squeezed into the other

parts.note: an aerial sends or receives radio signals

explanation.surface: Instructions to block a broadcast mast somewhere along a road.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: an arterial road is a main road, named after the body's big blood vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A main through route is called an arterial road, by analogy with the body's major blood vessels.

clue.text: A politician smitten with excite ment about the Colosseum

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament
smitten is an old past participle of smite, meaning hit
heat is excitement or passion, as in the heat of the moment
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An MP falls in love with the grandeur of ancient Rome's arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smitten' looks like 'in love' but is a word for struck. The page broke 'excitement' across a line, which is why it shows as two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum in Rome is the most famous example of an oval open-air arena with tiered seating.

clue.text: Laborious volume about lubricants

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the book word surrounds the oils

parts.note: a tome is a large book or volume
oils are used as lubricants

explanation.surface: A heavy book on engine grease makes hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laborious involves toil, hard and tiring work.

clue.text: Characters united in such writing…

parts.note: characters here are letters of the alphabet, and in this kind of handwriting they are joined to one another as the pen runs on

explanation.surface: A remark on a style of script, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' suggests people in a story, but here it means written letters, which are joined up in this flowing style.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined-up handwriting, with letters linked in a flowing line, is the standard name for this style of script.

clue.text: … namely, crude student scribble

parts.note: SC is short for scilicet, Latin for namely
raw means crude or unrefined
L is a learner, the letter on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a rough piece of handwriting by an untrained pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: SC (scilicet) is a crossword convention for 'namely'; L for student comes from the British L-plate shown by learner drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy hurried handwriting is a synonym for careless scribbled writing.

clue.text: This unscrupulous dealer upset people of high standing

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: VIPs are very important people

explanation.surface: A shady trader annoys the important guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns VIPS round to give the dealer; in a down entry this means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiv is British slang for a flashy petty crook trading in black-market goods, especially in the 1940s.

clue.text: Change outlook of soldiers in entire formation

indicators.note: a formation is an arrangement, so these letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops in full parade formation turn to face a new direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' rearranges OR plus ENTIRE. OR (Other Ranks) is a crossword convention for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorient is to shift your perspective or adjust your attitude in a new direction.

clue.text: Release articles in French about seizure of power

indicators.note: about here means around, so the two French words enclose the takeover

parts.note: un and le are French articles, indefinite and definite
a coup is a sudden seizure of power

explanation.surface: A French text about a government overthrow gets published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Release' is a verb, to detach, not a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncouple railway carriages is to detach them and let them go free.

clue.text: Prevent prizes being given back

indicators.note: given back suggests a return, so the word for prizes is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: pots are trophies or prizes, such as silver cups

explanation.surface: Blocking trophies from being returned to their winners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being given back' turns POTS round.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to halt it or block it from happening.

clue.text: Save shilling for ale, becoming rather drunk

indicators.note: becoming means turning into something else, so these letters change into a new arrangement

parts.note: SH is an abbreviation for the old British shilling coin

explanation.surface: Spend your coins on beer instead of saving, and you end up tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges SAVE, SH and FOR ALE. The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin worth 12 pence.
explanation.definitionFit: This old naval phrase describes someone well on the way to being intoxicated.

clue.text: Honour one's mother, initially standing for it.

definitions.text: Honour one's mother, initially standing for it.

parts.words: Honour one's mother, initially standing for it.
parts.note: the first letters of one's mother are O and M, and those initials stand for a British honour

explanation.surface: Respect your mum, at first standing up for her.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of 'one's mother' are OM, the post-nominal initials of this exclusive British honour, limited to 24 members and given by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a British order of chivalry awarded personally by the sovereign for distinguished service.

clue.text: One way to feed a small relation in a restaurant

indicators.note: to feed something into a piece is to put it inside, so the brother word takes the others in

parts.note: bro is a shortened form of brother, a relation
I is the Roman numeral for one
ST is an abbreviation of street, a way

explanation.surface: One method of giving a young family member dinner when eating out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' signals the shortened form of brother.
explanation.definitionFit: A small informal French-style eating place serving simple meals.

clue.text: Formally approve girl I arrange to meet

parts.note: Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie
to date someone is to arrange to meet them romantically

explanation.surface: Seeking official consent to go out with a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To validate is to confirm or ratify something officially.

clue.text: It alerts doctor, bishop, general and retired agent

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the agent word is read backwards

parts.note: a rep, a representative, acts as an agent

explanation.surface: A list of people summoned by some alarm: medic, cleric, officer, former spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns REP into PER. The definition is 'It alerts doctor': a pager that summons a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager carried by hospital staff beeps to call a doctor to an emergency.

clue.text: Resent move involving, for instance, rook

indicators.note: involving means taking in or enclosing, so the word for move surrounds the others

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly
EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for instance
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: Feeling bitter about a chess move that involves a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge is to feel envious or reluctant about something another person has.

clue.text: Horse-drawn vehicle needed for a jollification after church

indicators.note: after says the jollification comes later in the word than the church

parts.note: a riot can be a wildly enjoyable occasion, as in a riot of fun

explanation.surface: A carriage is needed for a party following the church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled vehicle pulled by horses, used in ancient racing and warfare.

clue.text: An intellectual's lofty summit

parts.note: lofty means high
the brow of a hill is its top or summit

explanation.surface: A scholar's lofty peak of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'has': the intellectual has the lofty summit as wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A highbrow is a person of refined cultural or scholarly tastes.

clue.text: Music from green in our village, ultimately

indicators.note: in says the colour word is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of village

explanation.surface: Music drifting from the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes E from 'village', giving OURE; 'in' puts VERT inside it after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an orchestral piece played at the start of an opera or ballet.

clue.text: Score about half a dozen, being uninspired

indicators.note: about means around, so the cut surrounds the number

parts.note: to score is to cut a line, to slash
VI is the Roman numeral for six

explanation.surface: Getting around six marks out of twenty for a dull piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests twenty, but here it means a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavish work imitates closely without any originality.

clue.text: Acceptable supply of fuel, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be pronounced and the matching word written

parts.note: a grate full of coal is a supply of fuel for a fire

explanation.surface: A welcome delivery of fuel, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you 'grate-full' sounds like the answer. 'Acceptable' is an old sense, as in a grateful shade on a hot day.
explanation.definitionFit: In older English the word meant pleasing or welcome, something received with pleasure.

clue.text: One day a transport organisation will serve the convent

parts.note: Fri is short for Friday
RY is an abbreviation of railway

explanation.surface: Some day a transport company will operate a service to the nunnery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convent' is used in its older general sense of a religious community, which includes houses of friars.
explanation.definitionFit: A friary is a religious house where a community of friars lives.

clue.text: Foreman gives retired judge cigarette

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so both words together are read backwards

parts.note: a ref, referee, judges a game
fag is British slang for a cigarette

explanation.surface: A works boss hands a cigarette to a judge who has stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'retired', turns the whole pairing round. FAG is everyday British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is British slang for a boss or the supervisor of a work crew.

clue.text: Matilda was amazing!

parts.note: in Hilaire Belloc's cautionary verse Matilda told such dreadful lies that no one would credit her when her house caught fire

explanation.surface: An exclamation of admiration for a girl called Matilda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazing' looks like praise, but it describes how incredible Matilda's lies were in Belloc's poem; she perished because nobody believed her.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond belief is incredible, the way Matilda's stories were.

clue.text: Engaged policeman

definitions.meaning: occupied or tied up, like a phone line in use

explanation.definitionFit: A word meaning occupied with work also serves, in old British slang, for a plain-clothes detective.

clue.text: Drive off egghead from the course

indicators.note: from says one piece is taken away from the other

parts.note: a route is a course or way
the head, or first letter, of egg is E

explanation.surface: Chasing an intellectual away from the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual, but it is the first letter of 'egg'; 'from' removes that E from ROUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rout an enemy is to defeat them and force them to flee.

clue.text: Oddly, Gray's writings generate a good deal of heat

definitions.text: generate a good deal of heat

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

parts.note: an author's works are his writings

explanation.surface: Surprisingly, the poet Gray's output is fiercely controversial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like 'strangely' but picks G, A and S from GRAYS. The definition is loose: the plant makes fuel that does what the phrase says.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant producing town gas makes the fuel that people burn to warm homes and cook.

clue.text: Artillery piece with zero manoeuvrability

indicators.note: manoeuvrability means being able to move freely, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A big gun that can be steered with no effort at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvrability' rearranges WITH ZERO.
explanation.definitionFit: A howitzer is a short cannon firing shells at a high angle.
